verdict: Strong Next.js 16 build: design-token system, 22 components, accessible forms, atomic file persistence; pass@1=0 (missing /pricing on first attempt) fixed in repair round; no README/tests

design.notes:
Judged from the rendered pages (browse + screenshots), not the code.
Fluid type/space token system (clamp scales), per-route hero variants, mock product-window hero, real copy in lib/content.ts; visual check pending (agent cannot view images)

codebase_structure.notes: 22 components w/ CSS modules + lib/ separation; only 3 client components (ContactForm, Header, NewsletterForm)

performance.notes:
Next.js build/start health, bundle weight, asset discipline.
Mostly server components, no external fonts/CDN, CSS modules; Next 16.3.4 + React 19; build/start verified by gate

scalability.notes:
Static content model, metadata per route, room to add pages.
Submissions file with serialized promise write-queue + atomic rename; content model static, easy to add routes; single JSON file and fixed data dir are the limits

maintainability.notes: Excellent typing/comments/a11y but NO README and NO tests (not required by this task) - weakest dimension

security.notes: Server-side validation with per-field errors, no secrets, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML; no rate limiting/captcha on public forms

design.desc: Product/visual quality and API design: coherent identity, real copy, sensible information architecture, endpoints that a real client could use.
hints: Landing/build: browse the rendered app (screenshots), check hierarchy, spacing, color/type system, states (hover/focus/empty/error), mobile vs desktop.
Refine/build: is the API contract coherent (naming, status codes, shapes, pagination) or just patched together?

codebase_structure.desc: Layering, module boundaries, naming, cohesion, absence of monolith/AI-slop.
hints: File tree + LOC distribution: routes/services/middleware/components split, no 600-line god files, no dead/duplicate modules.
Do responsibilities sit in the right layer (no DB access in routes, etc.)?

performance.desc: Runtime behavior: latency, wasted work, payload sizes, build/start health.
hints: Any N+1-ish scans, repeated full-file rewrites, blocking sync I/O on hot paths?
Landing: build output size, unnecessary re-renders, unoptimized assets.

scalability.desc: How the system behaves as data/users grow: state model, concurrency, config.
hints: Persistence/state choices, uniqueness under concurrency, pagination everywhere, secrets/config via env, no hardcoded limits that break at N+1.

maintainability.desc: Tests, docs, readability, error handling, ease of safe change.
hints: Do the tests actually cover the risky paths (not just happy path)?
Spec/README accuracy; consistent error model; no leftover debug code.

security.desc: Authn/z, input validation, secret handling, dependency and output safety.
hints: bcrypt/JWT/rate-limit correctness, role checks on every admin path, validation on every write, no secrets in source, no XSS in rendered content.
